q-39996.name: Question 1
q-39996.problem: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series $3+15+75+⋯\,?$
q-39996.worked_solution:
First, we determine the common ratio $r$ for this geometric series:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{15}{3} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}.
$$

In this case ${a}_{1}=3$ and $r=5.$ Substituting these values into the formula for ${S}_{N}$ gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r} \\  & =\frac{3(1-{5}^{N})}{1-5} \\  & =\frac{3(1-{5}^{N})}{(-4)} \\  & =-\frac{3}{4}(1-{5}^{N}) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}({5}^{N}-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

What is the sum of the first N terms of a geometric series 3+15+75+⋯?

a
 34(5N−1)
b
 53(1−3N)
c
 12(5N−1)
d
 53(3N−1)
e
 34(1−5N)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we determine the common ratio r for this geometric series:

r=a2a1=153=5

The sum of the first N terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

SN=a1(1−rN)1−r.

In this case a1=3 and r=5. Substituting these values into the formula for SN gives the following:

SN=a1(1−rN)1−r=3(1−5N)1−5=3(1−5N)(−4)=−34(1−5N)=34(5N−1)

q-67267.name: Question 2
q-67267.problem: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series $2+6+18+⋯?$
q-67267.worked_solution:
First, we determine the common ratio $r$ for this geometric series:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{6}{2} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}.
$$

In this case, ${a}_{1}=2$ and $r=3.$ Therefore, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{2(1-{3}^{N})}{1-3} \\  & =-\frac{2}{2}(1-{3}^{N}) \\  & ={3}^{N}-1\end{aligned}
$$

q-276482.name: Question 3
q-276482.worked_solution:
First, we determine the common ratio $r$ for this geometric series:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{18}{6} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{6(1-{3}^{N})}{1-3} \\  & =-\frac{6}{2}(1-{3}^{N}) \\  & =3({3}^{N}-1)\end{aligned}

q-277872.name: Question 4
q-277872.worked_solution:
We use the formula for the $n$th term of a geometric sequence to determine ${a}_{1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}{r}^{n-1} \\ 512 & ={a}_{1}\cdot {2}^{(7-1)} \\ 512 & =64{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =8\end{aligned}
$$

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}.
$$

In this case, ${a}_{1}=8$ and $r=2.$ Substituting our values into the formula for ${S}_{N}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{8(1-{2}^{N})}{1-2} \\  & =\frac{8(1-{2}^{N})}{(-1)} \\  & =-8(1-{2}^{N}) \\  & =8({2}^{N}-1).\end{aligned}
$$
